finding.claim: wipe() discards the boolean result of requireRole(u, "OWNER"), so the destructive repo.wipe(tenant) runs for any authenticated caller regardless of role.
finding.source: User u (caller identity and roles) and tenant path parameter on POST /tenants/{t}/wipe; precondition: caller is authenticated.

trace.note: Route comment: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe maps to wipe(User u, String tenant)
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as a statement; boolean result ignored

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (boolean predicate, not enforcing at this call site); checkRole at src/Admin.java:18 (throws, but not called in wipe; export at line 32 uses it); upstream/framework authorization not in repo, unverified. Open question, not a finding: tenant is not bound to u (User has global roles only), so cross-tenant wipe/export is possible if roles are global; needs role model to confirm.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-15) returns a boolean and never throws, and it is called as a bare statement at line 26 with the result discarded, so line 27 repo.wipe(tenant) runs unconditionally. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) does throw, but it is not called in wipe(); it only guards export() at line 32. No other code in the repo (only src/Admin.java exists besides skill docs) enforces authorization on the route.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls the boolean-returning requireRole(u, "OWNER") as a statement without checking its result, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any caller that reaches the route, which the trace describes accurately. Upstream route authentication is outside the repo and is not verified, but the in-repo check does not block a non-OWNER caller.
